basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 9.' and it opens '(Vers. 9.) Adorabunt te filii patris tui. Catulus leonis Juda, ex germine, fili mi,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 9.) Adorabunt te filii patris tui. Catulus leonis Juda, ex germine, fili mi, ascendisti, procumbens ut leo, et quasi catulus leonis. Quis suscitabit eum? Licet de Christo grande mysterium sit, tamen juxta litteram prophetatur [Al. interpretatur], quod reges ex Juda per David stirpem generentur, et quod adorent eum omnes tribus. Non enim ait, filii matris tuae, sed filii patris tui. Et quod sequitur, ex germine, fili mi, in Hebraeo habet, de captivitate, fili mi, ascendisti; ut ostenderet eum captivos populos esse ducturum: et juxta intelligentiam sacratiorem, ascendisse in altum, et captivam duxisse captivitatem (Psal. LXVII). Sive quod melius puto, captivitas passionem, ascensus resurrectionem signat.
